name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO)
handles: Takes complaints of housing discrimination under the Fair Housing Act, which bars discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, or disability.
complaint_process: File a complaint with FHEO online or by calling 1-800-669-9777.
evidence: File a complaint with HUD’s Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO)

name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
handles: Funds local Public Housing Agencies that run public housing and Housing Choice Vouchers, and takes complaints about HUD-assisted multifamily housing.
complaint_process: Public housing and voucher residents should contact their local Public Housing Agency or HUD's PIH Information Resource Center at (800) 955-2232. Residents of HUD-assisted apartments can call the Multifamily Housing Complaint Line at (800) 685-8470 (TTY (800) 432-2209).
evidence: HUD gives funding to local Public Housing Agencies (PHAs), which manage the Public Housing program.

name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) – Report Environmental Violations
handles: Takes online tips about possible violations of environmental laws and forwards them to EPA enforcement staff or the appropriate regulator.
complaint_process: Submit the online tip form. For an environmental event that may pose an immediate threat, call 911, then report it to the National Response Center at 1-800-424-8802.
evidence: report what appears to you as a possible violation of environmental laws and regulations

name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region 1 (EPA New England)
handles: EPA's regional office serving Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Vermont, and 10 Tribal Nations.
address: 5 Post Office Square - Suite 100, Boston, MA 02109-3912
evidence: Serving Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Vermont and 10 Tribal Nations

name: Social Security Administration (SSA)
handles: Assigns Social Security numbers and runs the Social Security retirement, survivors, disability, and Supplemental Security Income programs.
evidence: run the Social Security retirement, survivors, and disability insurance programs

name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services – Medicare (1-800-MEDICARE)
handles: Medicare's contact center answers questions by phone or live chat 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, except some federal holidays.
complaint_process: State Health Insurance Assistance Programs (SHIPs) can help people with Medicare file a complaint or an appeal.
evidence: You can talk or live chat with a real person, 24 hours a day

name: U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
handles: Investigates discrimination complaints against schools, school districts, colleges, universities, libraries, and other educational entities covered by laws OCR enforces.
complaint_process: File through the OCR Complaint Assessment System online, with the PDF complaint form, or by contacting the OCR enforcement office serving your state.
evidence: Contact the enforcement offices if you wish to file a complaint

name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
handles: VA's main information line (MyVA411) helps Veterans find the right VA phone number for health care and benefits.
evidence: Find the phone number to call for the help you need.

name: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
handles: Investigates safety defects in motor vehicles and takes vehicle safety complaints.
address: 1200 New Jersey Ave., SE, West Building, Washington, DC 20590
evidence: investigates safety defects in motor vehicles

name: Federal Transit Administration (FTA), U.S. Department of Transportation
handles: Helps state and local governments plan, carry out, and finance public transportation projects.
address: 1200 New Jersey Ave., SE, Washington, DC 20590
evidence: seeks to improve public transportation by assisting state and local governments

name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)
handles: Takes complaints about financial products and services and sends them to the company for a response.
complaint_process: Submit a complaint online. CFPB forwards it to the company, and most companies respond within 15 days. If another agency can help more, CFPB sends it there.
evidence: Submit a complaint about a financial product or service

name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
handles: Works to prevent fraudulent, deceptive, and unfair business practices, and helps consumers spot and avoid scams.
evidence: works to prevent fraudulent, deceptive, and unfair business practices

name: USAGov – Find and contact elected officials
handles: Points residents to names and contact information for their federal, state, and local elected officials.
evidence: Get the names and contact information for the people who represent you

name: USAGov Contact Center
handles: Live agents answer questions about federal benefits, programs, and services, or direct callers to the agency that can help.
evidence: direct you to an agency that can

name: U.S. House of Representatives – Find Your Representative
handles: Matches a ZIP code to its congressional district and links to the member's website and contact page.
evidence: matching your ZIP code to your congressional district

name: U.S. Senate – Contacting U.S. Senators
handles: Lists contact information for senators by state. Public policy questions and requests for personal help should go to your own state's senators.
complaint_process: Use the web contact forms on senators' websites, or mail The Honorable (Name), United States Senate, Washington, DC 20510.
evidence: requests for personal assistance should be directed to the senators from your state
